brief: 059 Sky's calls on S1-S3 (2026-10-25): S1 = no. Motive defines the rule that holds the final fight, and prices it
author: Motive

sky: S1, 2026-10-25: "no, it's to demonstrate the features of the games" (brief 059 'Sky's calls on S1-S3'). S2 yes and S3 run stand as built (rulings.json M059-5.1, M059-2.3).

howToRead: As rulings.json: kind value | rule | refusal | check | supersede; key is a proposal and Keel names the final path; every entry is proposed: true until Sky plays it. The two values are switches, so a later call is a value change: fight-always 0 and rivals-floor 0 give back the old pick (leave unfought).

entries.reason: Sky's S1: the Handover always shows its final fight. 1 = the final fight cannot be skipped: Go with Vale waits for the fight (M059-S1.2) and the crew refills to its floor (M059-S1.4). 0 = §06's hold alone, which was the old pick: a cell gone before anyone holds the car leaves unfought. One value, so Sky's later call is a value change. A generated mission can set it per mission: the capstone shows the feature, and a later mission may let preparation skip it.
entries.src: brief 059 'Sky's calls on S1-S3' 1; GDD v0.25 §07 final fight ('always, however fast or prepared the cell')

entries.value: With fight-always 1, from the final fight's start until it is over, Go with Vale aboard is refused while the fight's blocker is not out (down or gone, a rival blocker broken with his crew, §06). The refusal stays car-held, and its ids name the holders. (1) The blocker holds the car wherever he stands while he is up, not only on his lane post. (2) Before a blocker is named, whoever is coming holds it: car:rivals (safe; the answer carries its stop tick plus the step-out) or the officers still on their way (loud). The fight is over when every hostile is down, broken or gone, or, with no able crew left, as M059-S1.5. The §06 hold (within 8 m or on the exit lane) applies as before on top. Go without Vale (withdrawing by car) is not gated, and neither is the menu's Withdraw.
entries.reason: This is the only rule that closes leak (a). The rival car can't be on the map before 2:35.3 (GDD §07), and a cell can have Vale in a yard car at 2:22.5, so no timetable change makes the bodies arrive first. It reuses what the player already reads: Go's lock names its holders, and the rival car's approach line counts down to its stop (Glyph, brief 059 §1). It adds no new act: board and go (down the blocker, board, Go, Standing 0) and fight it out (+1) stay the two choices. The blocker becomes a must-down, which every shipped win already does: all 23 c037 wins Go after blocker.out, and with the gate on all 41 c037 scripts replay with the same final hash. It also closes M059-5.4's loud race at the yard (the cell's 6.5 s against the officers' 7.5 s), because the loud blocker must be down whatever the race. Preparation still pays: the gated yard (2:59.7) beats the square for A-pressure (3:20.5) and G-fast (3:11.0).
entries.src: GDD v0.25 §06 getaway (the hold, the blocker, Go), §07 final fight; probe results.txt §2 (41/41 same), §3 apress-gate, gfast-gate

entries.value: The spring is as built: the Enforcer with Vale, not inside, within fight-ambush-m 20 m of the stand's car, or Vale already in the car. The blocker is picked at the spring from the crew on foot. If none is on foot then (the crew still in the rival car, 059 F6), he is picked at the tick the first one steps out, among those on foot (ties by id). Each later arrival alerts as he steps out and fires aimNew (1 s) after. While no blocker is named, M059-S1.2(2) holds the car.
entries.reason: Pulse's F6 says 'a rider still in the car at the spring is not a candidate until he is out', but it doesn't say when a blocker is picked if no one is out. Without this, a yard spring before 2:52.1 would pick no blocker, and the gate would wait on a holder that never comes. 'Or Vale in the car' covers a spring condition that can't otherwise hold once Vale is aboard.
entries.src: briefs/059/pulse/rival-routine.md §6 F6, §7 (the spring, the blocker); probe engine-probe.patch (picks at the first step-out)

entries.reason: §07's floor ('3-5 hostiles'), kept as a count of real bodies. The rule (rivals.recall): at the safe fight's start, count the crew members that are able (up, not bound) and coming (posted, walking, in the rival car, or due back during the fight). If fewer than rivals-floor, away members come back, the earliest at the stand first (ties by id), until the count reaches the floor or nobody away is left. (1) The tipped car cuts its tip short, re-enters at rival-car-entry, and rides to the stand's rival stop; W steps out after rivals-out-s 5 s (Yard: entry to rival-tail 14.8 s, so W is on foot 19.8 s after the fight starts). (2) The warned lookout walks back from rival-lookout-exit to the stand's 4th spot (to rival-tail 34.7 m, 21.7 s). A knocked-out member who wakes during the fight rejoins as a joiner (M059-3.4). A killed or bound member is never replaced, and nothing spawns: the floor is 3, or every able member if fewer are left. Fiction: the crew calls its car by radio when a man doesn't answer (voice, 1950s). Readability: the car comes back on its approach line with the 'Rival car coming' card (rivals.back). A takedown on a posted rival that would bring the floor into play shows it on its line (Glyph and Fable: one mark, the car with a return arrow, no sentence). 0 = no recall.
entries.src: GDD v0.25 §07 final fight (3-5 hostiles); brief 059 §2.2 (the tip, the warn); rival-routine.md §7 (the wheelman returns into a running fight); probe g-thin1, g-thin3, gff-thin1; mission points rival-car-entry, rival-lookout-exit, rival-tail

entries.value: If no crew member is able (every one of the five killed or bound, and no knocked-out one due to wake before the cell is gone), the safe fight is over at once and the gate is open. The debrief records it as 'the crew was destroyed', so the cell fought them, piecemeal. Not reachable quietly. W never leaves the rival car before the fight, except in route B's tail when no tip was given (he walks to Vale's door, 6:38.9), and crew in a car are no takedown target (M059-3.1). So it takes five permanent takedowns on a busy square and in the Office's yard, each charged when found or reported.
entries.reason: Without this, a cell that has really killed all five would wait for a blocker that never comes (a softlock). Keeping it named, measured and unreachable on every reference route is the honest form of 'always'.
entries.src: GDD v0.25 §06 the hold ('a combatant not down, broken or gone'); rulings.json M059-3.1, M059-3.2

entries.value: A crew member who sees one of his crew taken down (in his cone, on a clear line, within his weapon's max ring) draws and fires on the taker. That is gunfire before the final fight (A >= 2, M059-3.3's public fight), and the final fight is loud. Finding a crewmate's body draws nothing (rivals don't report). It counts toward the recall at the fight's start.
entries.reason: §06 already fails a takedown on an armed target who sees it coming. This extends the same rule to his armed friends, so thinning by hand is priced by where the three stand. Pulse F7 leaves 'a member shot or taken down' to Motive. The posted pair at the square (ambush-1 and ambush-3, 2.3 m apart) can't be thinned quietly. A lone post can, and the floor then brings a late arrival, not nobody.
entries.src: GDD v0.25 §06 takedown (armed: fails, a fight), hostiles (rivals' cause: drawn, Vale, seen); rival-routine.md §6 F7

entries.value: No new code. car-held's ids may now hold car:rivals (with until = its stop tick + rivals-out-s) or an officer still running in, and the blocker wherever he is. Fable's line for the rival car: 'Rivals coming · 18 s' (the seconds from until). For the blocker the existing holder line is enough. Drive stays refused once the fight has started (M059-2.2), so the wait can't be driven out of.
entries.reason: Readable: one lock and one place to look. The reason is a body or a car the player can see on the map, with its seconds.
entries.src: GDD v0.25 §06 Go ('the refusal names the holders'); rulings.json M059-2.2; Glyph brief 059 §1 (approach line), §3 (shut stand)

keel: S1-GATE-EARLY-YARD: getaway car at service-drive, Vale aboard before 2:35.3. Go is refused car-held with ids [car:rivals] until the first rider steps out at rival-tail; then refused naming the blocker until he is down; then taken. Go at or after blocker.out.
S1-GATE-SWITCH-OFF: the same start with fight-always 0. Go is taken at Vale-aboard (the leak) and the fight never springs.
S1-GATE-C037: every c037 script with the gate on: the same outcome, tick and final hash (probe: 41/41).
S1-GATE-LOUD-YARD: route B taken at Alert 2. Go refused until the police blocker is down (closes M059-5.4's race).
S1-SPRING-LATE: the spring with nobody on foot. The blocker is picked at the first step-out (rival-1, ties by id), and each arrival fires aimNew after stepping out.
S1-FLOOR-TIP: tip, warned lookout, P1 knocked out. At the fight's start the tipped car re-enters at once, W steps out at the stand's rival stop 19.8 s later (yard), count 3.
S1-FLOOR-LOOKOUT: no tip, warned lookout, P1 and P2 knocked out. W comes by car (F6 Parked) and L walks back from rival-lookout-exit, count 3.
S1-FLOOR-NO-SPAWN: P1-P3 killed, tip, warn. W and L are recalled, count 2, and no hostile id beyond rival-5 exists.
S1-FLOOR-WAKE: P1 knocked out more than 2:00 before the fight. He rejoins his post and no recall is made.
S1-FLOOR-ZERO: rivals-floor 0 with the S1-FLOOR-NO-SPAWN start. No recall; with fight-always 1, crew-wiped holds only when no one is able.
S1-CREW-WIPED: all five killed. The fight is over at its start, the gate is open, and the debrief line reads 'crew destroyed'.
S1-SEE-TAKEDOWN: rival-1 (ambush-3) knocked out in rival-2's cone (ambush-1, 2.3 m). rival-2 fires, gunfire, A >= 2, the final fight is loud.

open: GDD §07 says '3-5 hostiles'. With the posted three killed or bound, and W and L the only ones left, the fight is 2. The floor can't make a third body without a spawn. Proposed §07 wording for Aster: '3-5 hostiles; fewer only when the cell has killed or bound crew members before it'. §06 the hold gets one line: 'in a mission that always fights (fight-always), the blocker holds the car wherever he is until he is out, and before he is named, whoever is coming holds it'.

The yard's ambush spots (Vantage): svc-ambush-1 is 5 m from the service door. Three posted at svc-ambush-1..3 shoot the carrying Enforcer down unless the cell focus-fires (probe g-posted3 at will: rivals-reach-vale at 3:22.0). Five at svc-ambush-1..5 kill him even with focus fire, but 059 never posts five. Waymark's re-record decides whether svc-ambush-1 moves off the door's line (a level change, not a rule).
